findings.reason: Both authentic standalone source tiles contain only prose/formulas. A concrete picture of nested closed rays materially clarifies the half-open interval convention, especially when a or b is an atom. The illustration directly explains proof step 1.1 without replacing any argument.
findings.action: Added one fenced TikZ number-line illustration and explanatory caption in final Remarks.

correction: Appended Remarks illustrating (-infinity,b] minus (-infinity,a] = (a,b], with open a, closed b and the interval-mass increment formula. Existing title, Statement, Facts, Proof and all frontmatter are byte-identical.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Borel probability measure mu on R; its CDF F:R to [0,1]; real a<b.
checks: The upper ray ends closed at b and the middle ray ends closed at a; both extend left, consistent with (-infinity,b] and (-infinity,a].
The dashed guides align a and b across the rays and baseline; a is geometrically left of b.
The difference interval has an open ring at a and filled point at b, giving exactly (a,b], including possible atomic mass at b and excluding possible atomic mass at a.
The displayed relation mu((a,b])=F(b)-F(a) is Statement parts 1/2 and proof step 1.1 via the finite-measure set-difference supplier.
The caption F(x)=mu((-infinity,x]) matches the local CDF definition and Statement part 2. Right-continuity and the 0/1 tail limits are restated without imposing continuity or excluding atoms.
There are no additional map, commutativity or graph claims. The rigorous phase proof is unchanged and independent of this figure.
